declared.title: Error rates for high confidence eyewitness identifications
declared.foundIn: OpenAlex search « confidence-accuracy characteristic analysis eyewitness high confidence identifications accurate meta-analysis » (2026-11-23)

population: eyewitnesses in actual criminal investigations tested by blind lineup administrators (field data), plus lab studies

findings.text: In real police lineups run blind, about 1 in 8 high-confidence identifications were known errors (an innocent filler picked)

support.sentence: This analysis shows that when eyewitnesses were tested in the field by a blind lineup administrator, 1/8 of the high confidence identifications were known errors, i.e., mistaken identifications of lineup fillers.

findings.text: In lab studies, error rates of high-confidence identifications of the suspect range from 0 to 40%, depending on how biased the lineup is against the suspect

support.sentence: Our claim is also supported by lab data, which show that error rates for high-confidence identifications of the suspect can range from 0 to 40%, depending on the level of bias against the suspect.

limits: filler picks are the only errors that can be known in the field: the true error rate is unknown, and most high-confidence picks were not known errors
the number of studies and countries are in the full text (not read)
about recognizing a stranger's face, not about remembering events of one's own life
a synthesis: the field part is a new meta-analysis (observational data), the lab part a non-systematic review
